Question B-007-008-004.

Why the correct answer is right: High frequency (HF) scatter can arrive through several redirected paths. When those delayed and shifted components combine in the skip zone, the audio can sound smeared or distorted.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "Auroral activity and changes in the Earth's magnetic field": Aurora can make very-high-frequency (VHF) signals raspy, but it is not the normal cause of HF scatter distortion in a skip zone.
- sourceIndex 2: "Propagation through ground waves that absorb much of the signal": Ground waves do not put multiple HF sky paths into the skip zone. They are surface-following signals that die out with distance.
- sourceIndex 3: "The state of the E-region at the point of refraction": Naming the E region misses the usual HF skip-zone mechanism: several F-region-related scattered paths can arrive with different delays and phases, so one region's state is not the source of the smeared audio.
